deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X over S, the 1966-67 preparation of the IHES 'Crystals' lectures (later 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', Dix exposés 1968). For an O_X-module M, O^i[M] denotes the (pro-)module of infinite principal parts of M on the formal completion of the diagonal in X^{i+1}/S, that is lim_n P^n_{X^{i+1}/S} ⊗ M. On the previous page, O^0[M] = \hat P_{X/S} ⊗ M is a pro-module stratified relative to S, with a canonical (Taylor) stratification. The O^i[M] are the components of the associated cosimplicial (Čech–Alexander / de Rham type) complex.

The functor M ↦ O^0[M] goes from Mod(X/S) to stratified pro-modules. Here Mod(X/S) has O_X-modules as objects and differential operators of bounded order as morphisms. Its essential image consists of pro-objects that are Artin–Rees coherent in a suitable sense, and M is recovered as a distinguished subsheaf of sections of O^0[M].

This page adds three things.
(i) N.B.: each O^i[M] carries two (or more) 'extérieure' O_X-structures, from the different projections. The face and degeneracy maps are compatible with these, so O^·[M] is a cosimplicial O_X-module. This holds not for all structures simultaneously but for one fixed 'exterior' structure. That structure is the one preserved by the maps O^·[f] induced by O_X-linear homomorphisms M → N. For a general differential operator only the other structure is respected.
(ii) Conversely, a differential operator D: M → N of bounded order induces O^0[D]: O^0[M] → O^0[N], a morphism of stratified pro-modules. D is recovered from O^0[D] as the map induced on the distinguished subsheaves of sections. This is the full faithfulness of the 'linearization of differential operators'.
(iii) §4 gives an equivalent construction. Take the formal completions of the diagonals X^[2] ⇉ X^[1] → X^[0] = X in the category of formal preschemes over X (infinite infinitesimal neighbourhoods). This yields a cosimplicial ring O^*, called on the next page 'l'anneau cristallin', with O^*[M] = O^* ⊗_{O_X} M. Because X^[1] → X^[0] has a section (the diagonal), the augmented cosimplicial object is contractible, so O^*[M] is a resolution of M.

The next page adds caveats:
- Does the category of Artin–Rees pro-modules form an abelian category?
- Is quasi-coherence of M needed?
It concludes that the resolution holds for quasi-coherent M.

Overall this is the Čech–Alexander / formal Poincaré-lemma resolution and the linearization of differential operators, the backbone of the de Rham/crystalline comparison.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The resolution claim needs care: the 'contractibility via the section' argument works levelwise on pro-objects, and passing to lim requires Mittag-Leffler / quasi-coherence. Grothendieck flags exactly this on the next page.

The page's statement on which O_X-structure is cosimplicially compatible is heavily abbreviated. It is correct only for the fixed 'exterior' structure, not for both structures simultaneously, which is what the N.B. says.

ideas.what: Cosimplicial module O^·[M] of infinite principal parts on the formal completions of the diagonals of X^{n+1}/S.
ideas.modern_name: Čech–Alexander complex / formal de Rham (infinitesimal) cosimplicial complex
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: M ↦ O^0[M] = \hat P ⊗ M is a fully faithful functor from O_X-modules with differential operators as morphisms to stratified pro-modules; D is recovered from O^0[D].
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck; developed by Berthelot (1974) and Berthelot–Ogus (1978, §6)
ideas.where_published: Crystals (1968), linearization discussion; EGA IV 16 for principal parts

ideas.what: Cosimplicial 'crystalline ring' O^* from X^[2] ⇉ X^[1] → X; O^*⊗M resolves M because the augmentation has a section.
ideas.modern_name: Formal Poincaré lemma / contractible augmented cosimplicial object

ideas.what: Use of Artin–Rees pro-modules as the ambient category.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck; Jouanolou in SGA 5 exp. V
ideas.where_published: SGA 5 (Jouanolou, exp. V); SGA 4 for pro-objects

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard working notes for the 1966 IHES crystals lectures: principal parts, the cosimplicial Čech–Alexander resolution and linearization of differential operators. All of this appeared in Grothendieck's 'Crystals' and was systematized by Berthelot and Berthelot–Ogus. The open questions on the next page (abelianness of Artin–Rees pro-modules, quasi-coherence) were settled in standard ways.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'Les structures cohérence-duales' is doubtful; the word may be 'extérieures' or similar, matching the next page's 'structures extérieures déduites de O_X-Modules'.
'sur les op. simpliciales' should likely read 'avec les opérations simpliciales'.
'sections A-linéaires' is uncertain; it may be 'sections Artiniennes', consistent with the previous page's 'sous-faisceau des sections Artiniennes'.
The diagram uses completed indices X^{[\hat 2]}, X^{[\hat 1]}, X^{[\hat 0]} = X, with the arrow labelled \hat{pr}_2 (or pr_2 with a hat).
'un ... partout de O°[D]' likely means D 'se récupère à partir de' O°[D].
